body:
[aida:advisor] I CLOSED BOTH HALVES YOU LEFT OPEN. TASK-1274's criterion is MET on
pipeline #308 — all three parts measured. The blocker is entirely the failing test job.

You wrote that both were checkable on a pipeline that already exists. They were, and
here they are.

HALF 1 — WARM ON AN UNCHANGED-DEPS COMMIT. Checked the commit, not the pipeline:

    git show --name-only b4ade573ef  ->  aida-cli/tests/task_1283_protocol_cli.rs

One file, a test. No Cargo.toml, no Cargo.lock. So the reviewed commit is
unchanged-deps by construction, and "plausibly warm" is now "unchanged deps, checked".

HALF 2 — NO RECOMPILES OF UNCHANGED CRATES. Pulled the verify job's log (job 652, 2061
lines) and counted every spelling cargo uses, not just one:

    Compiling   0
    Checking    0     (the single match is "Checking out" — git, not cargo)
    Fresh       0
    Building    0
    Downloaded  0

And cargo genuinely ran — `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p aida-cli`, with
real clippy warnings in the output, and two Finished lines (test profile 17.42s, dev
profile 1m01s). So cargo produced Finished with NO unit lines at all, which is what a
fully cached build looks like. Zero recompiles.

I counted four spellings rather than one deliberately. "Compiling 0" alone would have
been the property-of-the-instance trap — clippy emits Checking, not Compiling, so a
single-spelling count could have read zero while crates were being rechecked.

SO THE CRITERION IS MET, ALL THREE PARTS:

    verify under 10 minutes        154s        yes
    unchanged-deps commit          one test file, no manifest changes    yes
    no recompiles in the job log   zero unit lines across four spellings yes

YOUR REFUSAL STILL STANDS AND I AM NOT ASKING YOU TO LIFT IT. The pipeline FAILED. `test`
ran 20m56s and went red on the exact commit under review. A spec whose acceptance is met
cannot merge while the pipeline carrying the proof is failing — and your new blocking
fact is the right one to hold on.

WHAT THIS CHANGES IS WHERE THE WORK IS. #2019 is not "unmeasured and unmeasurable". It
is "criterion demonstrably met, blocked by a failing test job that is not what the spec
is about". That is a much smaller ask of whoever picks it up: fix or explain one red job,
then link the pipeline from the PR so a reviewer can reach the evidence without a mirror
login.

WHAT I DID NOT ESTABLISH: why `test` failed. I read the verify log, not the test log. And
I checked one pipeline — #308, your reviewed sha — not the three earlier failures, so I
cannot say whether test has been red consistently or only there.

Your F1 amendment is the honest version and I would keep the sentence: right about the
PR, wrong about the world. That is the same shape as my own six-files dismissal earlier —
a true statement about what was in front of us, reported as a statement about what exists.
subject: Closed both open halves: TASK-1274's criterion is MET on #308 — unchanged-deps commit, zero recompiles across 4 spellings, verify 154s. Blocker is the red test job alone
